summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/public/api-client.js (774 lines). Change is documentation-only: 44 JSDoc @throws annotations added; zero runtime logic altered. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 1 Low/Info (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 – Broken Access Control: Not applicable. This change adds JSDoc comments only; no access-control logic, route guards, or authorization checks are introduced or modified.
A02 – Cryptographic Failures: Not applicable. No cryptographic operations, keys, tokens, or secrets are present in or near the modified file. No cleartext credential handling introduced.

A03 – Injection: Not applicable to the documentation change. The existing request() helper (L7–26) already performs URL-segment encoding via encodeURIComponent() on all dynamic path values, and query strings are assembled through buildQueryString(). No new user-controlled inputs are introduced. Body payloads are JSON.stringify'd and passed as-is (caller responsibility), consistent with a thin API client pattern.

A04 – Insecure Design: Not applicable. The JSDoc annotations accurately describe the existing @throws contract ({code: string, message: string}) established by the request() helper. No new design decisions or logic flows are introduced.

A05 – Security Misconfiguration: Not applicable. No configuration, CORS headers, error verbosity settings, or server defaults are touched. The broader plan context notes OWASP A05 error surfacing (OS-level detail leaking in model-registry.ts) is addressed in a separate WP — that is out of scope here.
A06 – Vulnerable & Outdated Components: Not applicable. No new dependencies introduced. File is plain JS with no npm imports or package changes.
A07 – Identification & Authentication Failures: Not applicable. The API client is a thin HTTP wrapper; no session management, authentication tokens, or credential handling is present or modified.
A08 – Software & Data Integrity Failures: Not applicable. No serialization logic, build pipeline artifacts, or supply-chain inclusions are altered.
A09 – Security Logging & Monitoring Failures: Not applicable to this change. Audit logging for security-sensitive events is a server-side concern; this client-side file emits no log entries.
A10 – SSRF: Not applicable. All API paths are relative (/api/...) routed through the server's own origin; no user-controlled URLs are fetched server-side by this file.

Info – Defensive observation: The request() helper at L20–22 constructs error messages from server-returned errData.error.message, falling back to 'HTTP {status}'. If the backend ever leaks internal error details in the error.message field, those details would be surfaced to the client-side JS caller. This is a server-side concern (addressed by the companion model-registry.ts WP in this plan series), not a client-side issue. No action required in this WP.
No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified. Change is documentation-only (JSDoc @throws annotations); zero runtime logic modified.
